issues.legal_issue: A dispute over a member’s letting of a flat does not touch a housing society’s business when the society has sold the flat and is no longer its landlord.
material_facts: The flat owner had acquired the flat from the housing society and was a member of it.
The owner let the flat to another society member, who disputed the owner’s claim that the occupation was only under a leave-and-licence arrangement.
The society was not the landlord of the flat after selling it to the owner.
The owner referred the dispute to the Registrar, whose nominee made an award concerning the occupants’ status.
issues.conclusion: The dispute did not touch the society’s business and was not referable to the Registrar under section 91(1)(b); the nominee therefore had no jurisdiction to decide it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 91(1)(b), 91(3) and 163(1) of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act apply to disputes touching the society’s constitution, management or business. “To touch” means to come in contact with; a member’s letting of a flat does not touch the society’s letting business merely because the society itself is empowered to let land or its bye-laws regulate members’ dealings. There must be a point of contact with the society’s business, which was absent once the society had sold the flat. The case was distinguished from Deccan Merchants Co-operative Bank Ltd. v. M/s Dalichand Jugraj Jain and others, [1969] 1 S.C.R. 887, on its different facts.

rule.if: dispute_between_society_members and owner_acquired_flat_from_society and owner_let_flat_to_another_member and society_not_landlord_of_flat

predicates.dispute_between_society_members: A dispute arose between members of a housing society.
predicates.owner_acquired_flat_from_society: The member who let the flat had acquired it from the society.
predicates.owner_let_flat_to_another_member: The owner let the flat to another member of the society.
predicates.society_not_landlord_of_flat: The society had sold the flat and was not its landlord when the letting dispute arose.

issues.definition: When members dispute a letting of a flat acquired from the society, and the society is no longer the landlord, the dispute is not referable to the cooperative Registrar.

issues.legal_issue: The cooperative-society dispute process does not displace the Rent Act’s provisions for matters covered by that Act.
material_facts: The occupants sued in the Small Causes Court, claiming that they were tenants protected by the Bombay Rent Act.
The flat owner contended that the occupants were licensees and relied on the nominee’s award.
The occupants challenged the Registrar nominee’s jurisdiction, and the courts below had treated the award and the cooperative-society process as affecting the Small Causes Court proceedings.
issues.conclusion: For matters covered by the Rent Act, its provisions rather than those of the cooperative-society Act should apply; the appeal was allowed and the matter was returned to the Small Causes Court for disposal according to law, without deciding whether the occupants were tenants.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the harmonising approach noted in Deccan Merchants Co-operative Bank Ltd. v. M/s Dalichand Jugraj Jain and others, [1969] 1 S.C.R. 887: the Bombay Rent Act and the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act are best harmonised by applying the Rent Act to matters it covers. The occupants’ tenant status remained disputed and was not finally determined by this Court.

predicates.rent_protection_claim_made: The occupants claimed that they were tenants entitled to protection under rent law.
predicates.small_causes_suit_pending: The occupants brought a suit in the Small Causes Court concerning their possession of the flat.
predicates.dispute_within_rent_act_scope: The matter in dispute falls within the scope of the rent law.

issues.definition: When occupants claim rent-law protection in a pending Small Causes Court suit and the dispute is within the rent law’s scope, the rent-law provisions apply.
